API Reference¶

Fitting¶

glmhmm.fit.compute_total_emissions(params: GLMHMMParams, x_b, y_b, x_mn, y_mn, x_nb, y_nb, x_gm, y_gm, x_gs, y_gs, gs_first, gs_last, gs_segment_ids) → jax.numpy.ndarray¶

Computes total log-likelihoods by summing across all active emission distributions.

glmhmm.fit.e_step(params: GLMHMMParams, data: GLMHMMData)[source]¶

Performs the E-step of the EM algorithm for GLMHMM.

Computes posterior probabilities (responsibilities) for states and transitions using the forward-backward algorithm. Processes all sequences in the dataset.

Parameters:

  • params – Current GLMHMM parameters.

  • data – Dataset containing all observation sequences and covariates.

Returns:

List of state responsibilities for each sequence.

Each element has shape (T_i, K) where T_i is the length of sequence i.

xis: List of transition responsibilities for each sequence.

Each element has shape (T_i-1, K, K).

total_lml: Total log marginal likelihood across all sequences (scalar).

Return type:

gammas

glmhmm.fit.fit_glmhmm(data: GLMHMMData, config: GLMHMMConfig, initial_params: GLMHMMParams | None = None)[source]¶

Fits a Generalized Linear Model Hidden Markov Model using the EM algorithm.

This is the main entry point for training a GLMHMM. It alternates between: - E-step: Computing state/transition responsibilities using forward-backward - M-step: Updating parameters to maximize expected complete-data likelihood

The algorithm continues until convergence (change in log-likelihood < tolerance) or the maximum number of iterations is reached.

Parameters:

  • data – GLMHMMData object containing: - Observation sequences for each emission type - Covariate sequences for emissions and transitions All sequences should have the same length within each list.

  • config – GLMHMMConfig containing: - num_states: Number of hidden states (K) - num_em_iters: Maximum EM iterations - tol: Convergence tolerance for log-likelihood - l2_reg_*: Regularization parameters for each distribution

  • initial_params – Optional GLMHMMParams object to initialize the model. If None, parameters are initialized randomly.

Returns:

Fitted GLMHMM parameters including:

  • log_pi0: Initial state log-probabilities

  • log_A or theta: Transition parameters

  • W_*: Emission weights for each active distribution

  • phi_negbin, alpha_gamma: Dispersion parameters if applicable

lml_history: List of log marginal likelihoods at each EM iteration.

Can be used to diagnose convergence.

Return type:

params

Example

>>> data = GLMHMMData(x_bern=[X1, X2], y_bern=[y1, y2], ...)
>>> config = GLMHMMConfig(num_states=3, num_em_iters=100, l2_reg_bern=1.0)
>>> params, lml_history = fit_glmhmm(data, config)
glmhmm.fit.m_step(params: GLMHMMParams, data: GLMHMMData, gammas: List[jax.numpy.ndarray], xis: List[jax.numpy.ndarray], config: GLMHMMConfig) → GLMHMMParams[source]¶

Performs the M-step of the EM algorithm for GLMHMM.

Updates all model parameters by maximizing the expected complete-data log-likelihood using the responsibilities computed in the E-step. Each emission distribution and the transition parameters are updated independently.

Parameters:

  • params – Current GLMHMM parameters.

  • data – Dataset containing all observation sequences and covariates.

  • gammas – State responsibilities from E-step, list of arrays with shape (T_i, K).

  • xis – Transition responsibilities from E-step, list of arrays with shape (T_i-1, K, K).

  • config – Configuration containing regularization parameters and other settings.

Returns:

Updated GLMHMM parameters with optimized emission weights, dispersion parameters, and transition parameters (theta or log_A depending on model type).

Emissions¶

glmhmm.emissions.bernoulli_glmhmm_loglikelihood(X: jax.numpy.ndarray, y: jax.numpy.ndarray, W: jax.numpy.ndarray) → jax.numpy.ndarray¶

Computes the log likelihood of the data under the parameters W

Parameters:

  • X – Design matrix, shape (n_trials, n_features)

  • y – Response data (binary 0 or 1), shape (n_trials,)

  • W – Weight matrix, shape (n_features, n_states)

Returns:

Log likelihood of the data, shape (n_trials, n_states)

glmhmm.emissions.gamma_glmhmm_loglikelihood(X: jax.numpy.ndarray, y: jax.numpy.ndarray, W: jax.numpy.ndarray, alpha: jax.numpy.ndarray) → jax.numpy.ndarray¶

Computes Log-Likelihood for Gamma GLM.

Model:

y ~ Gamma(shape=alpha, rate=beta) Mean mu = alpha / beta = exp(X @ W) [Log Link] Therefore, rate beta = alpha / exp(X @ W)

Parameters:

  • X – Design matrix

  • y – Response data (must be strictly positive)

  • W – Weights determining the mean

  • alpha – Shape parameter per state (controls dispersion/variance)

Returns:

Log likelihood of the data, shape (n_trials, n_states)

glmhmm.utils.find_best_permutation(true_params, fit_output)[source]¶

Finds the state permutation that minimizes the MSE between true and fitted parameters. Handles ‘base class’ alignment for transition weights (theta) automatically.

Parameters:

  • true_params (dict) – Dictionary containing true parameters.

  • fit_output (namedtuple) – Output from fit_glmhmm containing fitted parameters.

Returns:

The optimal order of states (e.g., (2, 0, 1)) permuted_fit (dict): A dictionary with the fitted parameters re-ordered to match truth.

Return type:

best_perm (tuple)
